what: ADP processes payroll and runs human-resources systems for companies. It calculates pay, withholds and files taxes, handles benefits and, for smaller firms, acts as the legal co-employer that takes on insurance and compliance.
customers: More than a million businesses, from very small firms to multinationals, mainly in the United States.
money: payroll, tax filing, time tracking and HR software by subscription
taking on payroll, benefits and insurance for small businesses as co-employer
interest earned on tax and payroll money held briefly before it is paid out
moat: Payroll is painful and risky to switch, tax filing in every US jurisdiction is hard to replicate, and decades of data make its systems accurate.
risks: Revenue tracks employment: a recession cuts the number of paid employees it processes
Interest on client funds falls when central banks cut rates
Newer cloud rivals compete hard for mid-sized companies
Pricing power is limited in a mature market
opportunities: Recurring subscription revenue and very high returns on capital make earnings unusually predictable
The co-employer business keeps winning small firms that cannot manage benefits alone
Decades of consecutive dividend increases support the shares
watch: Employment growth at its client base and the pace of new business bookings.
